entities.summary: Gaius Aufidius Victorinus was a Roman senator and general of the second century, playing a crucial role in the governance of Roman provinces and collaborating with prominent figures like Emperor Marcus Aurelius and advocate Marcus Cornelius Fronto. As a friend and son-in-law to these influential individuals, he leveraged his connections to secure twice consulship and governorship of various Roman provinces. Victorinus's tenure was marked by his efforts to maintain order and stability in the face of external pressures and internal strife. Despite his significance, his name has faded into relative obscurity, overshadowed by the more prominent legacies of his contemporaries. His legacy serves as a testament to the enduring importance of careful governance and diplomacy in shaping the course of human history.
